<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **22** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **43** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `67bf557f73711286ffb93c60c7019518887a5433` — the merge of head `1061045e49d4f7c5ed116c87cfe010d232f78614` into base `a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 67bf557f73711286ffb93c60c7019518887a5433 && git checkout 67bf557f73711286ffb93c60c7019518887a5433
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d 1061045e49d4f7c5ed116c87cfe010d232f78614 && git checkout -B drift-repro a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d && git merge --no-ff 1061045e49d4f7c5ed116c87cfe010d232f78614

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `368141040945d223d96ef1094b612afec96f43b5`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: yes

PR #37439 for card #37099 (epic #37000). Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes`, new public CLI surface). Read: the card body and all 11 comments (takeover 7184309245 included), epic comment 7183567323, the PR body, the net diff (14 files, +1770/−5), the head's check-runs, and source on `main` and on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on the head: every run concluded `success` or `skipped`; none failed, and no name appears twice with differing conclusions. `Check Changeset`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (10/10 shards) and `Build Docs` are all `success`. The CLI `tsc` the dev could not measure locally is covered by `TypeScript Type Check` and `Type Check · workspace`.

### ① Derived judgments

**Card acceptance**

- Fresh deployment, one source, existing rows, searchable after boot: met. `buildSourcesAtBoot` runs from `kernel:bootstrapped` after `provideEmbedder`; test "a fresh deployment with one source and existing rows".
- Two nodes, one build: met with a shared lock. `rebuildSource` takes `knowledge:build:SOURCE` with `waitMs: 0`; a boot build re-reads the state once it holds the lock. See S1 and S4 for the edges.
- A built source is not rebuilt at boot: met (`current` and `listed-documents` are not due).
- The operator entry rebuilds and reports: met on one node; see S2 for several nodes.
- Item 4, the cost in the docs: met (the warn callout in `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`); see S4 for one missing case.
- Container run: the PR body reports a two-kernel run; CI is green.

**The build lock's lease against long builds** (previous seat's point 1)

- A healthy long build keeps its lease: 60 s, renewed every 20 s, each renewal armed after the last settles. `LockHandle.renew` is required by the contract (`packages/spec/src/contracts/cluster-service.ts:141`), and both in-repo drivers (memory, Redis) implement it. This is the same pattern `service-job` uses (`cron-job-adapter.ts`, #31843).
- A crashed builder cannot leave the lock stuck: it stops renewing, and the key frees itself within 60 s. Its in-memory `running` record dies with the process.
- S1 (should-fix) — A lease can still lapse mid-build (the lock store unreachable for over 40 s, or a renewal that hangs), and the walk then continues unfenced: it only warns, never checks `isHeld()` between pages, and does not pass the fencing token down. A second node's boot pass can then build the same source. The result is double embedding spend, not a corrupt index (same document ids and hashes; generation stores take their own builder lock in `beginBuild`). The opposite edge also exists: a build whose embed call never returns renews forever, and nothing but a restart cancels it, while the same node refuses a second rebuild. Stopping the walk at the next page once the lease is lost, and a bound on a build, can be a follow-up row.

**Admin-only rebuild and status on every door** (previous seat's point 2)

- REST: `POST /api/settings/knowledge/rebuild` and `/index_status` are the only network door. `SettingsService.runAction` calls `assertPermitted(manifest, 'write', ctx)` before the handler lookup (`settings-service.ts:3949`), the route context is `enforced`, and the `knowledge` manifest sets both `readPermission` and `writePermission` to `manage_platform_settings` (`knowledge.manifest.ts:47-48`). An anonymous or non-admin caller gets 403 before either handler runs, so status leaks no source name.
- MCP: no door. The only non-test caller of `SettingsService.runAction` in the tree is `settings-routes.ts:472`; the MCP bridge's `runAction` is the object-action seam and does not reach settings actions.
- CLI: `os knowledge rebuild` and `status` call that REST route with a bearer token; they add no door.
- Actions: neither is registered as an object action (`engine.registerAction`), so the `/actions` routes do not serve them.
- In process: `rebuildSource` and `readIndexState` are on `KnowledgeService`, not on `IKnowledgeService`; an in-process caller is trusted, as it already is for `reindexSource`.
- No door is unguarded.
- S3 (should-fix) — No test in this PR pins the gate. `knowledge-build.test.ts` calls the handlers directly, so the whole authorization of an action that spends money rests on a manifest value in another package. One pin (an enforced context without `manage_platform_settings` is refused for both actions through `runAction`) would catch a later relaxation of that manifest's `writePermission`.

**Per-node build records against the card** (previous seat's point 3)

- S2 (should-fix) — Card item 3 asks that progress and the last result be "readable by the operator entry". The record is in memory on the node that ran the build and is gone on restart. Behind a load balancer `os knowledge status` reaches the building node only by chance, and `os knowledge rebuild` exits 1 as soon as a poll lands on another node, although the build continues and may succeed; a script reads that as a failure. The PR declares this, the server log carries the result on every node's own log, and the index state is read from the store and is the same everywhere, so it does not block. A follow-up row should either share the record or let the CLI fall back to the index state (`due` turning `current`).

**The field gate's `title` arm** (previous seat's point 4)

- Agreed: it is its own row. Retiring a security gate needs per-source proof at search time that the index was built under the current recipe, and this PR only makes the rebuild happen. The gate stays, so nothing is weakened here.
- S5 (should-fix) — No card number carries it. The dev report names "the epic seat" as carrier, and that seat has since signed off (takeover 7184309245). File the row and name its number in the PR body before merge.

**Docs**

- N1 (nit) — The pointer in `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` (previous seat's point 5, in the takeover's file surface as "if added") is optional. That page stays accurate: lines 575-577 say nothing runs a reindex on a schedule, which is still true. A one-line pointer to the new section would help.
- S4 (should-fix) — The cost callout misses one case. The default adapter is `memory`, which holds nothing after a restart, so every boot is a first build and sends the whole source to the embedding provider again; it is also per process, so each node builds its own. The same paragraph says "with several server nodes, only one builds a source", which holds only with a shared cluster driver: the memory lock is a per-process mutex (`cluster-service.ts:149`). One or two sentences fix both.
- S6 (should-fix) — `os knowledge rebuild` and `os knowledge status` are not in `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, the CLI reference that lists the other commands (for example `os mcp connect`, line 3838). The PR body declares the omission. It can ride the next push.

**Boot-time build**

- It does not block boot: the hook calls `void this.service.buildSourcesAtBoot()` and returns.
- It runs on every node; the lock and the re-read leave one builder (with a shared driver, see S4).
- No knowledge service mounted means no pass; `buildAtBoot: false` turns the pass off and keeps the operator rebuild. There is no `enabled` setting on the namespace to respect.
- An unconfigured embedder reads as `unreadable` or fails the build with a warning; nothing is claimed built.
- A source with `refresh.onRecordChange: false`, a `file` or `http` source, and an adapter that cannot say are all left alone.
- N3 (nit) — `buildSourcesAtBoot` documents "never rejects", but `listSources()` sits outside its `try`, and the call site has no `.catch`. A `.catch` on the `void` call closes it.
- N5 (nit) — A first build that crashed part-way (`building: true`, no fingerprint) reads as `new-fingerprint` ("built under another fingerprint"). It is still due, so only the sentence is wrong.

**Settings contribution**

- `contributeKnowledgeSettings` gains an optional third argument and registers the two actions only when the service is passed. The manifest, the `test` action, the embedder section and the Setup entry are unchanged, and a composition with no settings service still gets nothing. The new actions have no `action_button`, so the Setup page does not change; the PR says so.

**CLI**

- N2 (nit) — `os knowledge rebuild --no-wait` exits 0 after "started" even when the build then ends `not-run` (another node holds the lock). The help text could say that `--no-wait` does not report the outcome.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-knowledge` and `@objectstack/cli` is the right level. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: nothing a metadata author writes changes (`buildAtBoot` is a plugin option, `packages/spec` is untouched, `IKnowledgeService` is unchanged). AGENTS.md: `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`.
- `Clause-②: yes` is correct: new CLI commands, new exports, a new plugin option, two new settings actions. Per `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `yes` and `yes (widening)` read the same; the arm is optional and nothing is owed.
- Both lines are in the PR body and in the changeset body. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no BREAKING banner, migration or ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- One thing for a reader of the changelog: the boot pass is on by default, so an upgraded deployment with a never-built source sends that source to its embedding provider at the next boot. The card asks for exactly this, and the changeset's "What it costs" bullet says it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, the `title` arm is not retired: answered above (S5).
- Dev flag, build records are per node: answered above (S2).
- Dev flag, no Setup page button: accepted. The card asks for "at least the CLI".
- Dev flag, CLI pages not updated: answered above (S6).
- Dev flag, CLI `tsc` not measured locally: answered by the head's `TypeScript Type Check`, `success`.
- Dev flag, six prerequisite gates left to CI: `Lint & Repo Gates` and its legs are `success`.
- Handoff flag, the optional pointer in `protocol/knowledge.mdx`: answered above (N1).
- Overlap with #37102 (PR #37442) and #37004 on `knowledge-rag.mdx`, and #37442's coded 503 from `getAdapter`: the seat's to check at landing. On this head `readIndexState` catches a throwing `getAdapter` and reads `unreadable`, so the boot pass survives it.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The build reuses the existing paged walk unchanged apart from a progress callback; `readIndexState` asks the adapter for `indexStatus` or one entry of `listDocuments` (`limit: 1`).
- Security: the PR adds an authorization-relevant surface (two admin actions, one of which spends money and sends content to a third party). Every door was read and is gated; hence `Security-touching: yes`, with S3 as the open hardening.

No must-fix. S1 to S6 are should-fix: S4, S5 and S6 are small enough to ride the next push; S1, S2 and S3 can be follow-up rows if the seat prefers.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-0g9cij`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `368141040945d223d96ef1094b612afec96f43b5`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5: contract record 7184443506 reads PASS with six should-fix findings. Three are fixed in this PR (a security pin and two docs gaps). Three close as cards named in the PR body, following the maintainer's rule that non-blocking issues become follow-up cards.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 14 files (+1770/−5), `Fixes #37099`, `Clause-②: yes` (bare `yes` reads as widening), `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch. The PR was taken over by `ai-37000` (7184309245). `l1-face` is CLEAN: 41 success, 15 expected skip, 0 failed.
2. **Premise**: no door is unguarded. REST is the only network door, `SettingsService.runAction` checks `manage_platform_settings` before the handler lookup, and a non-admin gets 403 with no source name. The boot build does not block boot, and `buildAtBoot: false` turns it off. A crashed builder's lock frees itself within 60 s. There is no SQL push-down finding.
3. **Owed in this PR**:
   - **S3.** Pin the admin gate. A non-admin `rebuild` and `index_status` through the real `runAction` path answer 403 and name no source. Today authorization rests on `knowledge.manifest.ts:47-48` in another package, with no test here.
   - **S4.** In the docs cost callout, add two facts. The default `memory` adapter is empty after every restart, so every boot re-embeds the whole source on each node. "Only one node builds" holds only with a shared cluster lock driver; the memory lock is per process.
   - **S6.** Add `os knowledge rebuild` and `status` to `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`.
   **Cards, under #37099 or #37000, named in the PR body:**
   - **S1.** A lease that lapses mid-build only warns, and the walk goes on unfenced, so two nodes can build the same source (double embedding spend). A build whose embed call never returns renews forever.
   - **S2.** Build records live in memory per node. Behind a load balancer, `os knowledge rebuild` exits 1 when a poll lands on another node.
   - **S5.** The field gate's `title` arm gets its own row. Its named carrier has signed off.
   The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations**: N1 (the optional `knowledge.mdx` pointer; that page is still accurate). Nits for the same push if cheap: N2 (`--no-wait` exits 0 on a later `not-run`), N3 (`void buildSourcesAtBoot()` has no `.catch`, and `listSources()` sits outside the `try`), N5 (a part-built first build reads as `new-fingerprint`).
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: lease fencing goes to the S1 card, shared build records to the S2 card, and the `title` arm to the S5 card.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, default tier, `Security-touching: yes`. A same-head PASS with S3, S4 and S6 closed and S1, S2 and S5 carded, plus an **ACCEPT**, are owed. The area lands it. Coordinate the landing order with o5-A's #37004 and `ai-37000`'s #37442, which share `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `1061045e49d4f7c5ed116c87cfe010d232f78614`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: yes

Delta review of PR #37439 for card #37099 (epic #37000), on top of the record for head `368141040945d223d96ef1094b612afec96f43b5`. Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes`). Read: `git diff 368141040945d223d96ef1094b612afec96f43b5..1061045e49d4f7c5ed116c87cfe010d232f78614` (4 commits, 10 files, +229/−11, no rebase, no main merge), the PR body at this head, os-dev report 7185409049, cards #37465, #37466 and #37467, and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on the head: 42 `success`, 17 `skipped`, 0 failed, and one not yet concluded. `Check Changeset` appears twice: the run started 06:57:57Z concluded `success`; a newer run started 07:25:24Z (after the PR body was rewritten) was still `in_progress` on three reads. The newer run governs, so that gate has no verdict at the time of this record. The changeset file and both declaration lines are unchanged in kind since the run that passed, so no red is expected, but the seat confirms the newer run's conclusion before landing. `PR-body guards` also appears twice; both runs are `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

**Findings of the previous record**

- S1: carried — card #37465 (open). Its acceptance covers both edges: the walk checks the lease before each page and stops with a recorded result, and a build has a bound. The PR body names it. The behaviour on this head is unchanged and is stated in the docs warning that a renewal failure is logged.
- S2: carried — card #37466 (open). Its acceptance offers the two fixes the record named (a shared record, or the CLI falling back to the index state) and asks for a test on a poll that lands on another node. The PR body names it, and the new CLI reference states the limit.
- S3: closed. `knowledge-settings-contribution.test.ts` boots a real `LiteKernel` with `KnowledgeServicePlugin` and `SettingsServicePlugin` and drives `registerSettingsRoutes` and the real `SettingsService.runAction`. A member holding `setup.read` and `setup.write`, and a signed-in caller with no capability, get `403 SETTINGS_FORBIDDEN` on `rebuild` and on `index_status`; an anonymous caller gets `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`. Each case asserts the refusal carries neither the source id nor its label, and that none of the five service methods the handlers use was called. The admin control proves the same door then names the source, so "names no source" is not vacuous. The in-process case asserts `runAction` rejects an enforced member with `required: 'manage_platform_settings'`. The reported ablation (the manifest's `writePermission` set to `setup.write`: 6 red) is the right one. The gate itself is unchanged.
- S4: closed. The callout in `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx` now says the default `memory` adapter is empty after a restart, so every boot re-embeds the whole source on every node, and that one builder needs a shared cluster lock driver.
